weeks.title: Relational Algebra, SQL Joins & Window Functions
weeks.objective: Master INNER, LEFT, FULL joins, GROUP BY aggregations, and window functions (ROW_NUMBER, LAG, LEAD).

slides.title: SQL: The Universal Language of Enterprise Data
slides.content: Spreadsheets crash at 100,000 rows; SQL databases process 100,000,000 rows in milliseconds. Understanding relational algebra and indexing enables analysts to extract deep customer insights, transaction velocities, and commercial revenue breakdowns on demand.
slides.codeSnippet:
SELECT v.name, count(t.id) as transactions, sum(t.amount) as total_revenue
FROM venues v
LEFT JOIN transactions t ON t.venue_id = v.id
WHERE t.created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY v.id, v.name
HAVING sum(t.amount) > 50000
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC;
slides.keyTakeaway: Mastering relational queries transforms raw transaction tables into actionable executive intelligence.

slides.title: Window Functions: LAG, LEAD & Running Totals
slides.content: Traditional GROUP BY collapses rows into summaries. Window functions calculate running totals, moving averages, and month-over-month growth rates while preserving individual row granularity.
slides.codeSnippet:
SELECT date, daily_revenue,
  SUM(daily_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY date) as running_cumulative_revenue,
  LAG(daily_revenue, 1) OVER (ORDER BY date) as previous_day_revenue
FROM daily_metrics;
slides.keyTakeaway: Window functions calculate cumulative metrics without complex self-joins.

caseStudy.scenario: A database query taking 45 seconds to scan 10 million transactions is slowing down the executive dashboard. How do you optimize it?

options.text: Add a composite B-tree index on (venue_id, created_at) and review execution plan with EXPLAIN ANALYZE
options.explanation: Composite indexes enable index-only scans, reducing query latency from seconds to milliseconds.
Destroying historical data is never a solution.
Hardware restarts do not resolve unindexed table scans.

quiz.question: What does SQL stand for?
quiz.explanation: SQL is the universal language for querying relational databases.

quiz.question: What is the difference between an INNER JOIN and a LEFT JOIN?
options: INNER returns only rows with matches in both tables; LEFT returns all rows from the left table plus matching rows
LEFT only runs on left-handed computers
quiz.explanation: LEFT JOIN preserves all records from the left dataset regardless of match in the right table.

quiz.question: What does the SQL window function LAG() do?
options: Accesses data from a preceding row in the same result set without using a self-join
quiz.explanation: LAG() allows instant comparison with previous period values for growth calculations.

quiz.question: What does the EXPLAIN ANALYZE command do in PostgreSQL?
options: Executes the query and displays the actual execution plan with node costs and execution times
quiz.explanation: EXPLAIN ANALYZE reveals whether queries utilize indexes or perform costly full table scans.

quiz.question: What is a Primary Key?
options: A physical key to the office
A column containing unique values that identify each row in a database table
The first column in an Excel sheet
quiz.explanation: Primary keys guarantee entity uniqueness and relational integrity.

weeks.title: Cohort Analysis, Retention Curves & Churn Prediction
weeks.objective: Measure customer retention, Net Revenue Retention (NRR), and predictive churn modeling.

slides.title: Cohort Retention & The Retention Smile
slides.content: Customer acquisition fills the top of the funnel, but retention dictates terminal business value. Cohort analysis tracks groups of users who signed up in the same month (e.g. January 2026 Cohort). If retention flattens out into a horizontal line (or smiles upward via expansion revenue), the company has achieved true Product-Market Fit.
slides.keyTakeaway: A leaky bucket cannot be scaled: fix retention before expanding ad spend.

slides.title: Net Revenue Retention (NRR)
slides.content: NRR measures the percentage of recurring revenue retained from existing customers over a period, incorporating upgrades, expansions, and cancellations. An NRR above 115% means the business grows exponentially even with zero new customer acquisition.
slides.keyTakeaway: Elite SaaS and subscription companies operate with NRR > 120%.

practicalLab.title: Lab 2: Build a Retention Cohort Matrix in Python/Pandas
practicalLab.brief: Ingest 100,000 customer transaction events and generate an unstacked heatmap matrix tracking monthly retention decay curves.

caseStudy.scenario: A company boasts that its customer base grew from 1,000 to 10,000 users this year, but its Net Revenue Retention is 65%. What is the true diagnosis?

options.text: Severe churn masked by aggressive ad spend; 35% of revenue is leaking every year, which will collapse when ad spend pauses
options.explanation: Low NRR indicates severe product churn hidden by heavy front-end acquisition spend.

options.text: The business is doing phenomenally well
options.explanation: 65% NRR represents an unsustainable leaky bucket.

options.text: They need to spend more money on ads
options.explanation: Accelerating spend into a churn-heavy product burns capital.

quiz.question: What is a Cohort Analysis in data analytics?
options: Tracking the behavior of a specific group of users who share a common characteristic (such as signup month) over time
quiz.explanation: Cohort analysis isolates behavioral changes over time across specific user groups.

quiz.question: What is Customer Churn Rate?
options: The percentage of customers who stop doing business or cancel their subscriptions over a specific period
The rate at which customers discover a company
The amount of profit per customer
quiz.explanation: Churn rate tracks lost customer accounts over time.

quiz.question: What does Net Revenue Retention (NRR) above 100% mean?
options: Revenue from existing customers is expanding faster than churn and downgrades, driving organic growth
quiz.explanation: NRR > 100% means existing accounts generate net expansion revenue without new customer acquisition.

quiz.question: What does a flattening horizontal line on a retention curve indicate?
options: Product-Market Fit: a dedicated core of customers retain indefinitely
quiz.explanation: A flattened curve indicates a baseline of permanent, loyal, non-churning users.

quiz.question: What is LTV (Customer Lifetime Value)?
options: The total net profit a business earns from a customer over the entire duration of their relationship
The time spent on the website
quiz.explanation: LTV quantifies the comprehensive enterprise value generated per customer.

weeks.title: Executive BI Dashboards, PowerBI & Visual KPI Modeling
weeks.objective: Build interactive C-suite dashboards, data modeling with DAX, and automated data refresh.

slides.title: Designing for Decision Makers, Not Vanity
slides.content: Bad dashboards display 50 cluttered charts that answer zero questions. Elite executive dashboards follow the 5-second rule: an executive should glance at the screen and immediately understand (1) Current Performance vs Target, (2) Root Cause of Any Variance, and (3) Required Corrective Action.
slides.codeSnippet: Dashboard Architecture: Macro KPI Cards at Top -> Trend Breakdown in Middle -> Actionable Anomaly Table at Bottom
slides.keyTakeaway: If a metric does not drive a specific business decision, eliminate it from the screen.

slides.title: PowerBI Data Modeling & Star Schemas
slides.content: Never dump one massive flat table into PowerBI. Professional data engineering structures models into Star Schemas: a central Fact Table (recording transactions with timestamps and numbers) surrounded by Dimension Tables (Customer, Venue, Product, Date) connected by 1-to-many relationships.
slides.codeSnippet:
Star Schema:
  Fact_Sales (amount, quantity, date_id, customer_id, venue_id)
    ├── Dim_Customer (customer_id, tier, nationality)
    ├── Dim_Venue (venue_id, name, district)
    └── Dim_Date (date_id, day, month, year, is_uae_holiday)
slides.keyTakeaway: Star schemas optimize DAX calculation speed and prevent circular relationship errors.

caseStudy.scenario: An executive complains that a dashboard takes 30 seconds to reload every time they click a filter. How do you resolve it?

options.text: Refactor the data model into a Star Schema, aggregate historical fact tables, and use import mode instead of live unindexed direct queries
options.explanation: Star schema modeling with indexed aggregations provides instantaneous sub-second interactive filtering.

options.text: Tell the executive not to click filters

options.explanation: Proper data modeling solves performance bottlenecks.

quiz.question: What is a Star Schema in data warehousing?
options: An architectural data model featuring a central numeric Fact table surrounded by descriptive Dimension tables
quiz.explanation: Star schemas optimize analytical query performance and dimensional slicing.

quiz.question: What is a Fact Table in a data warehouse?
options: A table containing verified true facts
A table storing quantitative measurements, metrics, and transaction foreign keys
quiz.explanation: Fact tables record atomic numerical business transactions (sales, clicks, logins).

quiz.question: What is DAX in PowerBI?
options: Data Analysis Expressions — the formula expression language used to create custom measures and calculated columns
quiz.explanation: DAX enables advanced mathematical calculations over dimensional data models.

quiz.question: What is the '5-Second Rule' in executive dashboard design?
options: A decision maker should understand current business performance and variance within 5 seconds of viewing the dashboard
quiz.explanation: Dashboards must present critical commercial signals with zero cognitive clutter.

quiz.question: Why are vanity metrics (like page views) dangerous when used for strategic decisions?
options: They look impressive on surface charts but have zero correlation with cash flow, net profit, or customer retention
quiz.explanation: Vanity metrics mask underlying operational decay and mislead executive leadership.

weeks.title: Dubai Open Data, Predictive Modeling & Capstone Forecast
weeks.objective: Leverage the Dubai Open Data Initiative, train predictive machine learning regression models, and project market demand.

slides.title: Dubai Open Data Initiative & Smart Dubai API
slides.content: Under the Dubai Data Law, government entities publish public datasets on Dubai Pulse and Dubai Data Portal: covering tourism arrivals, airport passenger flow, public transit footfall, and real estate transactions. Integrating these APIs allows businesses to forecast consumer demand 30 days in advance.
slides.keyTakeaway: Open data provides macro macroeconomic indicators to benchmark company performance.

slides.title: Predictive Forecasting with Python & Scikit-Learn
slides.content: Moving from retrospective reporting ('what happened') to predictive intelligence ('what will happen') requires training machine learning models (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, ARIMA time series) on historical seasonal trends, public holidays, and macro indicators to predict venue foot traffic.
slides.codeSnippet:
from sklearn.ensemble import GradientBoostingRegressor
model = GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=100)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
forecast_next_30_days = model.predict(X_future)
slides.keyTakeaway: Predictive forecasts optimize staff scheduling, inventory orders, and dynamic venue pricing.

options.text: A local public holiday or unexpected weather anomaly; retrain the model including federal holiday calendars and weather APIs as features
options.explanation: Machine learning models require relevant external shock indicators (holidays, weather) to capture non-linear demand shifts.
Engineering better input features fixes the prediction.

An open Wi-Fi network in malls

quiz.question: What is the difference between Descriptive and Predictive analytics?
options: Descriptive explains what happened in the past; Predictive models what will happen in the future using statistical learning
Descriptive is in English; Predictive is in Arabic
Descriptive is for schools; Predictive is for banks
quiz.explanation: Predictive analytics utilizes statistical models to forecast future outcomes.

quiz.question: What is an ARIMA model commonly used for?
options: Time series forecasting to model trends, seasonality, and cyclic fluctuations over sequential time data
quiz.explanation: ARIMA is a classical econometric time-series forecasting model.

quiz.question: What is Feature Engineering in machine learning?
options: Selecting, transforming, and creating the most predictive input variables from raw data to train algorithms
quiz.explanation: Feature engineering directly determines the predictive accuracy of machine learning models.

quiz.question: Under the Dubai D33 Economic Agenda, what is the role of digital data assets?
